When applied to “other gods,” the term “serve” refers to honoring them by living as their followers did, building shrines for them, and following religious practices such as praying to them and offering sacrifices to them. Bowing down to these gods (physically bowing to an idol that represented them in a shrine or temple) was a symbolic action of surrender to them as one’s lord. It represented a definitive further step, beyond the idea of “serving” or honoring them, that would provoke Yahweh’s judgment, as he describes in the following verses. So we recommend that you do not combine these two phrases in your translation. While their meaning is similar, there is a significant difference between them. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain in the text of your translation or in a footnote the significance of bowing down. Alternate translation: [and honor other gods and ultimately commit yourself to them by bowing down to them]

A **dowry** is a payment or transfer of money, property, or valuable goods by a woman’s family to her new husband or his family at the time of their marriage. Typically in the biblical culture, a man would instead pay a bride-price to the woman’s family. But some men, especially rulers such as Pharaoh, gave property or territory to their daughters when they were married. If your readers would not be familiar with what a dowry is, you could explain it in your translation with a general term or a descriptive phrase. Alternate translation: [as a gift to his daughter on the occasion of her marriage to Solomon]

The term translated as **completed** here is different from the term translated as “finished” in [9:1](../09/01.md). The author is not restating that Solomon had finished building the temple, even though he is concluding this account of Solomon’s building projects, and he often concludes an account with a review statement. Instead, he means that by offering these sacrifices on the occasions of Israel’s three great annual feasts, Solomon made the Jerusalem temple the center of Israel’s worship. The Israelites no longer worshiped at the high places, as the author notes in [3:2](../03/02.md) that they had been doing previously. If your language has different words for “finished” and “completed” that would convey these different senses, it would be appropriate to use them in your translation.
